learn.hook: At Jantar Mantar in Jaipur stands a giant sundial, the Samrat Yantra, built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II. Its shadow tells the time!
points: Long ago, people measured time using the Sun and natural events: the day, the phases of the Moon and the year.
Sundials use a moving shadow; sand clocks (hourglasses) use falling sand; water clocks, called ghatika in ancient India, used a bowl with a small hole that slowly filled and sank in water.
A simple pendulum is a small heavy ball (bob) hanging from a thread. One complete to-and-fro swing is one oscillation, and the time it takes is the time period.
For a pendulum of fixed length at a place, the time period stays the same. A longer thread gives a longer time period. That is why pendulums were used in clocks.
The basic (SI) unit of time is the second (s). 1 minute = 60 s, 1 hour = 60 minutes = 3600 s, and 1 day = 24 hours.

example.q: A pendulum makes 20 complete oscillations in 40 seconds. What is its time period?
steps: Time period = total time ÷ number of oscillations

learn.reallife: Today quartz watches and phones keep time very accurately, and atomic clocks, the most accurate of all, help satellites and GPS work.

quiz.q: What is the SI unit of time?
quiz.explain: The second (s) is the standard unit of time used by scientists all over the world.

quiz.q: What is the time period of a pendulum?
options: Time taken for half a swing
Time taken for one complete oscillation
quiz.explain: One oscillation is a full to-and-fro swing, back to the starting point. The time for it is the time period.
quiz.mistake: Counts half a swing as one oscillation

quiz.q: A pendulum completes 10 oscillations in 20 seconds. What is its time period?
quiz.explain: Time period = 20 s ÷ 10 = 2 s.
steps: Time period = total time ÷ number of oscillations
quiz.mistake: Divides the wrong way round or forgets to divide

quiz.q: How many seconds are there in 2 hours?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 60 only once

quiz.q: What happens to the time period of a pendulum if its thread is made longer?
quiz.explain: A longer pendulum takes more time to complete each swing.
quiz.mistake: Thinks length does not affect the swing

quiz.q: Which ancient Indian device measured time using a bowl with a small hole floating in water?
quiz.explain: The bowl slowly filled with water and sank after a fixed time, marking a unit of time.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the water clock and the sand clock

quiz.q: A sundial works because:
options: The shadow of a stick moves as the Sun appears to move across the sky
quiz.explain: As the Earth rotates, the Sun seems to move, so the shadow moves across marked lines.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up how different clocks work

quiz.q: How many minutes are there in 3 hours?
quiz.explain: 1 hour = 60 minutes, so 3 hours = 3 × 60 = 180 minutes.
quiz.mistake: Uses 100 or 10 minutes in an hour

learn.hook: A cheetah can sprint faster than a car on a city road, but a tortoise is happy to take its time. How do we compare how fast things move?
points: Speed tells us how much distance is covered in a unit of time.
The SI unit of speed is metre per second (m/s). For vehicles we often use kilometre per hour (km/h).
If an object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time along a straight line, its motion is uniform. Otherwise it is non-uniform, like a bus in city traffic.
For non-uniform motion we use average speed = total distance ÷ total time. A speedometer shows a vehicle's speed and an odometer shows the distance travelled.

example.q: A train travels 240 km from one city to another in 4 hours. What is its average speed in km/h?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time

learn.reallife: Road signs on highways show speed limits in km/h, and the Vande Bharat trains are known for their high speeds.

quiz.q: What is the formula for speed?
quiz.explain: Speed tells distance covered in each unit of time, so we divide distance by time.
quiz.mistake: Divides the wrong way round

quiz.q: Which is the SI unit of speed?
quiz.explain: Speed is distance per time, so its SI unit is metre per second.
quiz.mistake: Gives a unit of distance or time instead of speed

quiz.q: A boy runs 200 m in 40 s. What is his speed in metres per second?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies or adds instead of dividing

quiz.q: A bus travels at 50 km/h for 3 hours. How many kilometres does it cover?
quiz.explain: Distance = speed × time = 50 × 3 = 150 km.
quiz.mistake: Adds or divides instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Which of these is an example of non-uniform motion?
options: A toy car moving 1 m every second in a straight line
A toy train moving 2 m every second on a straight track
A car moving in heavy traffic
A ball lying still on the ground
quiz.explain: In traffic the car keeps speeding up, slowing down and stopping, so it covers unequal distances in equal times.
quiz.mistake: Does not understand what uniform motion means

quiz.q: A car travels 120 km in 2 hours, but stops and starts on the way. Its average speed in km/h is:
quiz.explain: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 120 ÷ 2 = 60 km/h.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies distance and time

quiz.q: Which instrument in a vehicle shows its speed?
quiz.explain: The speedometer shows speed. The odometer shows the total distance travelled.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up speedometer and odometer

quiz.q: A scooter moves at 72 km/h. What is this speed in metres per second?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change both kilometres and hours into metres and seconds

teach.ask: Gappu flew 100 metres in 20 seconds, and a pigeon flew 100 metres in 10 seconds. Who was faster, and how do we measure speed?
teach.praise: Chirp chirp! Speed = distance ÷ time. The pigeon was faster this time, but Gappu is practising!

learn.hook: A picture can tell a whole journey story! A distance-time graph shows at a glance whether someone was fast, slow or resting.
points: A distance-time graph shows time on the horizontal (x) axis and distance on the vertical (y) axis.
A straight sloping line means equal distance in equal time: uniform speed.
A steeper line means a higher speed: more distance in the same time.
A flat (horizontal) line means the distance is not changing: the object is at rest.
A curved line means the speed is changing: non-uniform motion.

example.q: Neha cycles to school. Her graph rises steadily for 10 minutes, stays flat for 5 minutes, then rises steadily again. What happened?
steps: Rising steadily means she was moving at a steady speed.
A flat part means her distance did not change: she was stopped.
Then the line rises again, so she started moving again.
example.answer: She cycled at a steady speed, stopped for 5 minutes (perhaps at a signal), then cycled again.

learn.reallife: Delivery apps and fitness bands track your distance over time and draw graphs like this to show your speed and rest breaks.

games.title: Match the graph to the story
Read the graph
items: In a distance-time graph, time is usually shown on the horizontal axis.
Time goes along the x-axis and distance goes up the y-axis.
A flat line means the object is moving very fast.
A flat line means distance is not changing, so the object is at rest.
A straight sloping line shows uniform motion.
Equal distance is covered in equal time, so the speed is steady.
Of two straight lines, the steeper one shows the slower object.
The steeper line covers more distance in the same time, so it shows the faster object.
A curved line shows that speed is changing.
When speed changes, the slope changes, so the line curves.

quiz.q: On a distance-time graph, what does a horizontal (flat) line show?
options: The object is moving very fast
quiz.explain: If the distance stays the same as time passes, the object is not moving.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a flat line means steady motion

quiz.q: What does a straight line sloping upward show?
quiz.explain: A straight sloping line means the same distance is covered in each equal time interval.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up straight and curved graphs

quiz.q: Two cars' graphs are straight lines. Car A's line is steeper than car B's. Which is faster?
quiz.explain: A steeper line means more distance in the same time, which means a higher speed.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a steeper line means slower

quiz.q: A car's distance is 40 km after 1 hour, 80 km after 2 hours and 120 km after 3 hours. What is its speed in km/h?
quiz.explain: It covers 40 km in every hour, so its speed is 40 km/h and its graph is a straight line.
quiz.mistake: Takes the total distance as the speed

quiz.q: In a distance-time graph, what is shown on the vertical (y) axis?
quiz.explain: Distance goes up the vertical axis and time along the horizontal axis.

quiz.q: Rahul walks 2 km in the first hour, rests for 1 hour, then walks 2 km more in the third hour. What is his total distance in km?
quiz.explain: He walked 2 km + 0 km + 2 km = 4 km. The rest hour adds no distance and shows as a flat part on the graph.
quiz.mistake: Counts distance during the rest hour
